question: What reliability caveats should be kept in mind when interpreting the cascade-versus-router comparison results?

Similarly, the live router numbers that look almost like perfect routing are also leakage [3]. The held-out set (64% savings) is the fairest test [2].

- Live cascade quality came in 2 points below the offline estimate, so offline numbers may be optimistic [3].
- Sample sizes are small. The held-out set has 100 questions, math has 50, and the disagreement finding rests on 11 wrong answers [1][2].
- Routing's value depends on how often the cheap model fails. On easy questions, Always Haiku was only 2 points below the router, so routing adds little [2].
- Rankings change with the quality tolerance. The best option differs across the ≤1%, ≤3%, and ≤5% rows [4].
- Latency results depend on hardware. The router was slower in the live replay because embeddings ran on a laptop CPU under load [3].
